plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, an inked chemical diagram shows calcium ions (Ca²⁺) triggering fibrin clotting in untreated blood within 4–6 minutes on touching glass, versus Luis Agote (9 Nov 1914) and Richard Lewisohn's (23 Jan 1915) 0.2% sodium citrate chelating Ca²⁺ ions to keep blood liquid for 14–26 days in Oswald Hope Robertson's November 1917 Western Front iced ammunition-box blood depot.

teach_overlay.label: 0.2% SODIUM CITRATE CHELATES CA²⁺ → 14–26 DAYS IN 1917 WWI ICEBOX
teach_overlay.detail: Inked diagram on period paper showing calcium-driven fibrin clotting in untreated blood (4–6 min) vs 0.2% sodium citrate chelating Ca²⁺ ions allowing 14–26 days of cold storage in Robertson's November 1917 Western Front icebox
teach_overlay.scale: storing Type O blood on ice in 1917 turned transfusion from a two-surgeon emergency operation into a bottle waiting at the front line
